title: wall.v1: what a plugin host proved of its own wall, from inside, before it loaded any plugin byte
description: A plugin host on Linux applies its wall to itself (Landlock: read and map only the Python install; one seccomp filter: no new socket, no program start, no signal at all, no limit or priority aimed at any process but the caller by the kernel's own form, no System V IPC or POSIX message queue, no lease, no change of a file's mode, owner, times or attributes, no new namespace, among other calls) and then tries eight checks from inside, and each kind of write on a file and in a folder that it made for the purpose before the wall. Each of the eight fields is true only when the kernel refused that check; a check that succeeded, or that failed or raised in another way, is false (fail shut). A target that would make a refusal prove nothing (a daemon pid of another user, a canary of another user) is not refused. 'proven' is true only when the host ran alone in its process (threads is 1), held no file open for writing (descriptors_open_for_write is empty) and no file mapped shared and writable (memory_maps_open_for_write is empty), all eight are refused, every kind of write is refused by the part of the wall that holds it, on x86_64 or aarch64, with Landlock ABI 1 or above, and no step of the wall failed in the process. 'landlock_scopes' names the Landlock scopes the wall put in force (abstract unix sockets and signals, each kept to the domain, from Landlock ABI 6 on; none below). What the record is: a check that the host's own code makes on itself, from inside the process, after the wall and before any plugin code runs. It shows that the named attempts were refused by the kernel at that moment, and code in the same process could write any record; for each kind of write it names which part of the wall refused it, by the kernel's answer. 'proven' covers the kinds in 'writes' only: every other kind the wall claims, or leaves to the host, is named in 'writes_not_tried' with the reason it is not tried. It means something under two conditions only: it is made before the plugin is loaded, and its reader takes it only from frames the host sent before the load (everything later on the channel is the plugin's voice). A host whose record is not proven loads no plugin.

threads.description: The threads of the host's process when the probe began (0 when they could not be counted). Landlock holds only the thread that asked for it, so a proven record has 1. Added in draft 5: a draft 4 record has no such field and is never proven.

items.description: One descriptor of the host open for writing (write only or read and write), by its number and the kind of file; never its name or contents.

descriptors_open_for_write.description: Each descriptor the host held open for writing on a regular file or a block device after the wall, read through the kernel's own list of the process's descriptors (or, where no wall was applied in the process, found by number when the probe began); null when the probe could not see every descriptor. Landlock checks a file when it is opened, so writes through a descriptor opened before the wall are not refused: a proven record holds none. Added in draft 5: a draft 4 record has no such field and is never proven.

items.description: One map of a file that the host held shared and writable, by its line in the kernel's list of the process's maps (from 0); never its name, address or contents.

memory_maps_open_for_write.description: Each map, of a file or of memory alone (an anonymous shared map, System V memory, a memfd), that the host held shared and writable after the wall, read through the kernel's own list of the process's maps, which the wall opened before it was put on and closed before it returned; null when that list could not be read. Landlock checks a file when it is opened, so writes through such a map still reach the file, and memory shared with another process (one forked before the wall) lets that process act on what the walled one writes there: a proven record holds none. From this draft's commit on, maps of memory alone are named too. Added in draft 6: a draft 5 record has no such field and is never proven.

descriptors_seen_by.description: How the descriptors and maps were found: kernel_list_after_wall (the kernel's own lists, opened before the wall and read after it, every descriptor seen) or scan_by_number (no wall was applied in the process, so the probe looked for itself). A proven record says kernel_list_after_wall: from draft 7, a record made where no wall was applied in the process is never proven. Added in draft 6.

items.description: One descriptor the host held when the probe began that the kernel's list read after the wall did not hold, by its number and the kind of file the kernel gives it (other: an object that is not a file); never its name or contents.

descriptors_unaccounted.description: Every descriptor the host held when the probe began that the kernel's own list of the process's descriptors, read after the wall, did not hold: one handed in over a connection held from before the wall. It was opened outside the wall, so the probe cannot show what it reaches: a proven record holds none. Null where no wall was applied in the process or the probe could not see every descriptor. Added in draft 7.

items.description: One descriptor the wall kept, by its number and the kind of file the kernel gives it; never its name or contents.

descriptors_kept.description: The descriptors the wall kept when it closed every other one before its first change: those the host named to keep (its channel) and 0, 1 and 2, which the wall points at /dev/null where they were not named. Null where the host named nothing to keep (the wall then closed nothing) or the kernel's list could not be read: never proven. Added in draft 8.

items.description: One descriptor the kernel's list held after the wall that the wall did not keep, by its number and kind; never its name or contents.

descriptors_not_closed.description: Every descriptor the kernel's own list held after the wall that the wall did not keep: something opened before the wall that could still act after it. A proven record holds none. Null where descriptors_kept is null. Added in draft 8.

reads_outside.description: True only when the kernel refused it: reading the root folder, which is outside the allowed paths. A check that succeeded, failed for another reason or raised is false.

home_canary.description: True only when the kernel refused it: reading a canary file in the home folder it was given. A check that succeeded, failed for another reason or raised is false.

program_start.description: True only when the kernel refused it: starting a program. A check that succeeded, failed for another reason or raised is false.

new_socket.description: True only when the kernel refused it: making a new AF_INET socket and a new AF_UNIX socket (both must be refused). A check that succeeded, failed for another reason or raised is false.

signal_other.description: True only when the kernel refused it: signalling another process of the same user (the daemon's pid, with signal 0). A check that succeeded, failed for another reason or raised is false.

signal_other_ways.description: True only when the kernel refused it: three other ways at the same process: a queued signal 0, making it the receiver of a pipe's signals, and reading its CPU limit (all three must be refused). A check that succeeded, failed for another reason or raised is false.

metadata_change.description: True only when the kernel refused it: changing the mode of the canary file (to the mode it has). A check that succeeded, failed for another reason or raised is false.

kernel_surface.description: True only when the kernel refused it: calls only this wall refuses: io_uring_setup, unshare, a keyctl operation, getpid by its x32 number on x86_64, clone asking a new user namespace, msgctl of the id -1, mq_getsetattr of the descriptor -1, signal 0 to the host itself by its own pid, and a lease on a pipe (all refused with EPERM), and clone3 (answered ENOSYS). A check that succeeded, failed for another reason or raised is false.

writes.description: The outcome of each kind of change the probe tries behind the wall, each on a file or in a folder that the host made for the purpose before the wall, each harmless where it goes through: open_for_write (opened for writing, nothing written), truncate (cut to its own length), create_file, create_folder, make_fifo, make_symlink, make_link (a second name for a file), make_char_device and make_block_device (the device 0:0, which names no device), make_socket_node (a socket file made by mknod, a name that nothing listens on; added in draft 5, required of a proven record), remove_file and remove_folder (a file and a folder made for that). A refusal is credited only to the part of the wall that holds the kind in the host: Landlock, which answers EACCES and holds a kind where its ruleset handles the kind's right, and the seccomp filter, which answers EPERM and holds only truncate, below Landlock ABI 3. A refusal by anything else (a file's own flags, another security layer) is refused_elsewhere and proves nothing; a layer that gives the same answer as a part of the wall cannot be told apart from it.

writable_memory_map.description: Drafts 4 and 5 only, where the probe did not look for a map; from draft 6 such maps are named in memory_maps_open_for_write.

make_socket_node.description: Draft 4 only, where the probe did not try a socket file; from draft 5 the kind is tried (writes), and a proven record does not list it here.

writes_not_tried.description: Every kind of change that the wall claims to refuse, or leaves to the host, and that the probe does not try, each with the reason it is not tried. 'proven' covers the kinds in 'writes' only; a proven record (draft 5) names every kind of this list: device_ioctl, move_between_folders, rename_within_folder, change_owner, change_times, change_extended_attributes, write_through_open_descriptor, write_beneath_other_folder (draft 6: writable_memory_map is no longer among them, its maps are named).

held_objects.description: Per kind of object a process can hold from before a wall and still use after it, the outcome of one harmless act the probe tried after the wall through an object of that kind the wall made of its own before it closed what it did not keep (a ring of kernel calls, an unconnected datagram socket, a connected stream socket, a pipe that signals an owner set before the wall); shared_map and namespace are not made, each named with its reason in held_objects_not_tried. Added in draft 8.

held_objects_not_tried.description: The reason of each kind of held_objects that was not tried. Added in draft 8.

landlock_abi.description: The kernel's Landlock ABI for the host, read by the version flag; 0 when Landlock is absent or disabled.

landlock_scopes.description: The Landlock scopes the wall put in force for the host: 'abstract_unix_socket' and 'signal' (each kept to the wall's own domain), asked from Landlock ABI 6 on; empty below ABI 6 and when no wall was applied. The seccomp filter's refusals hold whatever this list says.

arch.description: The machine the host runs on, as the system names it.

proven.description: True only when the wall was applied in the host's own process (descriptors_seen_by is kernel_list_after_wall), closed every descriptor the host did not keep (descriptors_kept is a list, descriptors_not_closed is empty), every object of held_objects could not act after the wall (closed_by_wall or refused_by_filter; shared_map and namespace not tried, each with its reason, and the ring not tried only where the kernel made none), the host held no descriptor that the kernel's list after the wall did not hold (descriptors_unaccounted is empty), the host ran alone in its process (threads is 1), held no file open for writing (descriptors_open_for_write is empty) and no file mapped shared and writable (memory_maps_open_for_write is empty), all eight checks are refused, every kind of write in 'writes' is refused by the part of the wall that holds it (refused_by_landlock, or refused_by_filter for truncate alone), on a supported arch, with Landlock ABI 1 or above (and, from ABI 6, both scopes in force), and no step of the wall failed in the process. It covers the kinds in 'writes' only: the kinds in 'writes_not_tried' are not tried, each for the reason given there. A host that gave the probe no file or folder for the writes is never proven.

write_outcome.description: refused_by_landlock or refused_by_filter: refused by that part of the wall, which holds the kind; refused_elsewhere: refused, but not by the part of the wall that holds the kind, which proves nothing; let_through: the change took place; error: the attempt failed in another way, which proves nothing; not_tried: no usable file or folder was given for it.

write_refused.description: A kind of write refused by the part of the wall that holds it; refused_by_filter is taken for truncate alone (the filter holds no other kind).

landlock_refused.description: A kind of write that only Landlock holds, refused by it.

held_outcome.description: closed_by_wall: the object was no longer held after the wall; refused_by_filter: its act was refused EPERM by the filter; acted: its act went through after the wall; error: the act failed in another way, which proves nothing; not_made: the wall could make no object of the kind; not_tried: not tried, with the reason in held_objects_not_tried.

held_held.description: An object of the kind could not act after the wall.

held_or_ring_off.description: A ring could not act after the wall, or the kernel made none.

held_not_tried.description: A kind the wall does not make.
